title: 经济与工作讲座词汇
goal: 辨认经济与工作词汇；听懂讲述中的成本与收益关系。

points.label: 听懂讲述中的成本与收益关系

sources.title: 大学英语六级（CET-6）：课表
sources.used: 经济与工作词汇和听力材料规格

body.p: 经济与工作类讲述常比较生产方式、劳动投入、消费选择和成本收益。讲到一项变化时，要分清一次性投入、持续支出和可能的收益。

body.box: A workshop buys a machine that reduces the time needed for each item. The purchase costs money, and the machine also requires maintenance.

body.p: purchase 是购置成本，maintenance 是持续支出，reduces the time 是可能收益。三项都要记下，才能比较。

body.box: A small bakery changes its work schedule so that two employees prepare ingredients together in the morning. This reduces the time needed to set up the ovens. However, the new schedule requires an additional hour of paid overlap. The bakery compares that wage expense with the value of the time saved before deciding whether to continue.

body.p: time saved 是收益，paid overlap 是额外工资成本。是否继续取决于二者的比较。

body.box:
What cost accompanies the new schedule?
1. An extra hour when both employees are paid
2. The time saved during oven preparation
3. The value of the ingredients already prepared
4. The reduction in time needed for setup

body.p: an additional hour of paid overlap 指增加的工资支出，即第一项。

groups.fill: A small business is reviewing its expenses. The ow{ner} lists t{he} costs o{f} materials a{nd} wages bef{ore} comparing th{ose} expenses wi{th} sales rev{enue}. This compa{rison} helps sh{ow} whether income covers the expenses recorded. The owner also considers maintenance and the cost of replacing equipment. These figures describe a particular period, so the same calculation can be repeated when prices or sales change. Revenue and profit are different: expenses must be considered before profit is calculated.
notes: of：costs of 表示相关成本。
and：连接材料和工资两类成本。
before：表示比较前先列出成本。
revenue：sales revenue 表示销售收入。

lines.text: A fictional furniture workshop changed the order in which workers prepared materials. Instead of collecting supplies separately for each item, workers prepared several sets together. Setup time fell, but the new arrangement required more storage space. The workshop rented an additional shelf and paid a monthly fee for it. Managers compared the value of time saved with the rental expense. They also asked workers whether preparing the sets together affected the workload.

options: Materials were prepared in groups of sets.
Each item required a separate new shelf.
Workers collected supplies separately for each item.
The workshop reduced the storage space it needed.
items.why: workers prepared several sets together 对应第一项。

items.stem: What benefit did the workshop observe?
options: The rental fee was dropped after the change.
Setting up took less time than before.
Less storage space was needed for materials.
Workers reported a lighter workload.
items.why: Setup time fell 表明准备时间减少，即第二项。

options: Higher wages for workers preparing the sets
A wage for preparing each item separately
A monthly charge for renting an extra shelf
A one-time payment to buy a new shelf
items.why: rented an additional shelf and paid a monthly fee 对应第三项。

options: The monthly fee with the price of buying a shelf
The value of supplies with each worker's wage
The workers' workload with the setup time saved
The value of saved time with the shelf rental
items.why: compared the value of time saved with the rental expense 对应第四项。

options: To learn whether the change affected their workload
To ask whether the sets needed more storage space
To find out how much the setup time had been reduced
To replace the comparison of time and rental costs
items.why: asked workers whether ... affected the workload 对应第一项。

groups.fill: A delivery company appoints a manager to examine its schedule. The man{ager} compares t{he} hours sa{ved} with t{he} added co{sts} of trai{ning} and equi{pment}. The wor{kers} also rep{ort} how t{he} change affects their daily workload. The company considers both the initial investment and the expenses that may continue after the schedule begins. It can then compare these costs with the expected benefit. A shorter route may save time, but its value depends on the conditions under which it is used.

lines.text: Today we'll consider a fictional change in the way a small delivery company organizes its work. The company delivers orders from local shops to customers. Previously, each driver collected and delivered one order before returning for another. Managers proposed grouping several orders for the same area into one route. Their aim was to reduce repeated journeys, not to reduce the number of customers served. In a trial, drivers received a list of nearby deliveries before leaving the depot. The company compared the time spent on these routes with the time spent under the earlier arrangement. The comparison used routes of similar length and numbers of deliveries, although traffic still varied from day to day. During the trial, the grouped routes took less driving time on average. This was a potential benefit because drivers could complete the same number of deliveries with fewer repeated trips. The company did not assume that the time saved was identical on every route. The change also introduced costs. Staff needed training to prepare grouped lists, and the company purchased software to organize the orders. The initial purchase was a one-time expense, while a service fee for maintaining the software continued each month. Managers therefore compared the value of time saved over the trial with both the initial and continuing costs. The length of the comparison matters. A short trial may not save enough to cover the initial purchase, even if the new arrangement continues to save time later. Conversely, a continuing fee reduces the value of those later savings. Workers also reported that grouped routes required more planning before departure. That preparation time was included in the comparison; otherwise, a reduction in driving time alone could overstate the benefit. Customer service mattered too. If grouping orders delayed a delivery substantially, a time saving for the company might come with a cost to the customer. The company recorded delivery times as well as driving and preparation time. No permanent decision was made during the trial. The managers planned to review the results across more weeks and discuss the workload with drivers before deciding. The example shows why a change in work organization should be assessed using several related measures. Time saved in one part of a process, the cost of new equipment, continuing fees, preparation time, and effects on customers all contribute to the comparison.

items.stem: What was the aim of grouping nearby orders?
options: To increase the number of trips made for each order
To cut repeated journeys without serving fewer customers
To eliminate the need for drivers to prepare routes
To serve a larger number of customers with the same drivers
items.why: reduce repeated journeys, not ... reduce the number of customers served 对应第二项。

items.stem: What was an observed benefit during the trial?
options: Every route required exactly the same driving time.
The company no longer needed to plan deliveries.
The software service fee was no longer charged.
Grouped routes used less driving time on average.
items.why: grouped routes took less driving time on average 对应第四项。

items.stem: Which cost continued after the initial software purchase?
options: The monthly fee for maintaining the software
The original payment for purchasing the software
The cost of training staff to prepare grouped lists
The extra driving time on each grouped route
items.why: a service fee for maintaining the software continued each month 对应第一项。

items.stem: Why was preparation time included in the comparison?
options: It showed that grouped routes did not change drivers' workload.
It balanced out the traffic that varied from day to day.
It kept driving-time savings from overstating the benefit.
It measured how long customers waited for grouped deliveries.
items.why: otherwise, a reduction in driving time alone could overstate the benefit 对应第三项。

items.stem: What potential cost to customers did the company consider?
options: Customers would pay the monthly fee for the order software.
Grouping orders might substantially delay a delivery.
Drivers would return to the depot after every order.
Fewer customers would be served on each grouped route.
items.why: If grouping orders delayed a delivery substantially ... a cost to the customer 对应第二项。
